english_paragraphs: On 10 April 1912 the opulent liner Titanic left Southampton on her maiden voyage. A 1911 trade journal had dubbed her and her sister ship "practically unsinkable". At about 11.40pm on 14 April she collided with an iceberg; by 2.20am she had vanished beneath the waves, and the death toll would surpass 1,500.

Folklore blames arrogance. Yet the Titanic was compliant with the law. Under 1894 rules, Britain's maritime regulator pegged lifeboat numbers to gross tonnage (volume, not weight) on a scale that topped out at 16 boats for 10,000 tons or more. At about 46,000 tons she carried 20, exceeding the requirement. Their capacity was 1,178, roughly half the 2,200 aboard: sufficient in law, inadequate at sea.

Within radio range, the steamer Californian kept an equally lawful routine. Her sole wireless operator, Cyril Evans, was on the payroll of the Marconi company; when he slept, so did the radio. Around 11.30pm he switched off his set. Hindsight may call that negligence, yet no rule obliged him to stay vigilant, so the Titanic's frantic distress calls went unheard there.

Between April and July 1912, inquiries in Washington and London heard testimony from survivors and the Californian's crew. That July, American legislation made round-the-clock radio watch compulsory. In January 1914 delegates of 13 nations signed the first Safety of Life at Sea convention, stipulating lifeboat seats for all, continuous radio watch, and an ice patrol. The First World War stalled the treaty; the patrol went ahead regardless.
The doomed liner sank within three hours. The outdated rules she sailed under had stayed afloat since 1894; it took her dead to discredit them.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 1912年4月10日，**豪华的**(opulent)**邮轮**(liner)泰坦尼克号离开了南安普敦，开始了她的**处女航**(maiden voyage)。1911年，一家**行业期刊**(trade journal)**把**(dubbed)她和她的姊妹船**称为**(dubbed)“**几乎**(practically)**不会沉没的**(unsinkable)”。4月14日晚约11时40分，她**和**(collided with)一座**冰山**(iceberg)**相撞了**(collided with)；到次日凌晨2时20分，她已**消失**(vanished)在海浪之下，**遇难人数**(death toll)最终将**超过**(surpass)1,500。

**坊间流传的说法**(Folklore)把灾难归咎于**傲慢**(arrogance)。然而泰坦尼克号**符合**(compliant with)法规。按照1894年的规则，英国的**海事**(maritime)**监管机构**(regulator)**把**(pegged to)救生艇数量**与**(pegged to)**总吨位**(gross tonnage)（体积，而非重量）**挂钩**(pegged to)，在一个**等级表**(scale)上/**等级体系**(scale)中，（其数量）**最高达**(topped out at)（只能）**到**(topped out at)16艘，针对10,000吨及以上（的船）。她约有46,000吨，带了20艘，**超出了**(exceeding)**要求**(requirement)。它们的**容量**(capacity)是1,178人，**大约**(roughly)是船上2,200人的一半：按法律**足够**(sufficient)，到了海上却**不足**(inadequate)。

在无线电通讯范围内，加州人号轮船遵循的是一套**同样**(equally)**合法的**(lawful)值班惯例。她**唯一的**(sole)**无线电**(wireless)**操作员**(operator)西里尔·埃文斯，**受雇于**(on the payroll of)马可尼公司；他一睡下，电台也一样睡了。晚上11时30分左右，他**关掉了**(switched off)自己的设备。**事后看来**(Hindsight)，这或许可称为**疏忽**(negligence)，然而没有哪条规则**强制**(obliged to)他保持**警觉**(vigilant)，所以泰坦尼克号**发狂似的**(frantic)**求救呼叫**(distress calls)，在那里**无人听见**(unheard)。

1912年4月至7月，华盛顿和伦敦的调查听取了**幸存者**(survivors)以及加州人号船员的**证词**(testimony)。同年7月，美国的一项**立法**(legislation)将**全天候**(round-the-clock)无线电值守定为**强制性的**(compulsory)（义务）。1914年1月，13国的**代表**(delegates)签署了第一部《海上人命安全**公约**(convention)》，**规定**(stipulating)救生艇座位要够所有人乘坐，电台要**不间断**(continuous)值守，还要开展冰情**巡逻**(patrol)。第一次世界大战让这项**条约**(treaty)**暂缓搁置了**(stalled)；然而冰情巡逻**不管怎样**(regardless)依然进行。
这艘**在劫难逃的**(doomed)邮轮不到三小时就沉没了。她航行时所遵循的那套**过时的**(outdated)规则，却自1894年起**一直没有沉没**(stayed afloat)；直到她的乘客葬身大海，它们才**信誉扫地**(discredit)。

sentences.chinese_source: 1914年1月，13国的**代表**(delegates)签署了第一部《海上人命安全**公约**(convention)》，**规定**(stipulating)救生艇座位要够所有人乘坐，电台要**不间断**(continuous)值守，还要开展冰情**巡逻**(patrol)。

sentences.english: The First World War stalled the treaty; the patrol went ahead regardless.
sentences.chinese_source: 第一次世界大战让这项**条约**(treaty)**暂缓搁置了**(stalled)；然而冰情巡逻**不管怎样**(regardless)依然进行。

sentences.english: The doomed liner sank within three hours.
sentences.chinese_source: 这艘**在劫难逃的**(doomed)邮轮不到三小时就沉没了。

sentences.english: The outdated rules she sailed under had stayed afloat since 1894; it took her dead to discredit them.
sentences.chinese_source: 她航行时所遵循的那套**过时的**(outdated)规则，却自1894年起**一直没有沉没**(stayed afloat)；直到她的乘客葬身大海，它们才**信誉扫地**(discredit)。

approved_summary: 1912年，号称几乎不沉的泰坦尼克号首航撞冰山，不足三小时沉没，逾1500人遇难。
旧规按总吨位（容积）定艇数，万吨以上只需16艇；它有20艇、1178座，仅够船上2200人约一半。
附近加州人号的唯一报务员关机休息并未违规，电台没听到求救；当时没有全天值守的强制规定。
1912年美国强制全天守听；1914年13国签约，要求全员救生艇座位、连续守听和冰情巡逻。
一战使公约搁置，冰情巡逻仍启动；沿用自1894年的旧规暴露出：合法配置，并不等于安全足够。
